It's a short puzzle game with platforming elements. Its puzzles are for the most part very mundane and its platforming is frustrating - poor controls, obnoxious visuals that distract and obscure hostile elements, and little grace leave little room for enjoyment if you ♥♥♥♥ up. the game also has a habit of hitching on a frame during certain segments of the platforming when attacking enemies even on a rig like mine which would have been considered high-end years after this game was released

In terms of narrative, its trite and dull. it attempts to do many "meta" aspects relating to the narrative, but was released after games that were already tackling similar meta-commentary on games far better - e.g., The Stanley Parable, The Beginner's Guide, and Undertale. All three achieve their aims and are much more compelling as games in terms of actual narrative complexity, emotionality, and the meta-commentary they actually put forward. it doesn't flesh out any of its characters and what writing they might have is boring and delivered agonisingly slowly.

Lastly, the visual aspect of the game is not only played-out but breaks the very scant rules and ideas it wants for its setting. its satanic and biblical imagery is some of the lowest-hanging fruit for a meta game like this i've experienced. it also clearly seeks to emulate old graphics, resolutions, and stuff like that, but fails at basically every metric because of the way it was designed:
  : : pixel sizes are inconsistent, never in scale with each other, and are able to freely rotate despite this just flatly not being possible 
  : : it uses a very weird pulsating faux-3D effect on text, giving it red and cyan shadows, despite the UI ostensibly trying to be diegetic
  : : there's a persistent overlay throughout the game replicating a strange rounded-rectangle screen, which was long out of use by the time of the graphics this game calls back to
  : : its diegetic elements imply it's a PC, but the game takes place on an arcade machine in an arcade
  : : it clearly seeks to make use of diegesis as part of its meta-commentary, including, admittedly, a singular interesting segment at the tail end of Act III, but is incredibly inconsistent with this diegesis, often ignoring it wholesale when and are it's convenient

from what i can gather, it was popular because it was popular on youtube when it was released. as a game, it's exceedingly mid. i guess on a technical level it's sufficient - it plays - but it plays poorly, is uninteresting, and uses a horror-style visual language for the sake of using a horror-style visual language only. nothing interesting is done visually, narratively, or thematically

相较于《邪恶冥刻》的层次性，《小马岛》的meta似乎粗糙又露骨，直白地将跳出循环的入口丢给玩家，全程渗透出一种低质量但迷人的诡谲气质。其核心的横板跳跃街机玩法是朴素的，惊喜感更多来自不稳定的未知，你明知这是诡计，却悬空着等待制作者的下一步出招。阻止游戏继续是它最大的游戏性，因此闪退可以是华丽收尾，卸载成了名正言顺的终极自杀进程。在带有自毁倾向的程序中，全收集反而会坠入无穷无尽的深渊，这或许也是撒旦的黑色玩笑。当看穿成为路径，溢出的0和1不过是路西法阴谋的一部分。以为跳出流程实际是在触发分支，看似破坏规则实际是在完成规则，以为识别诡计实则参与了诡计。而对于meta元素的思考最终都会回到这个问题：在游戏中玩家是否能够真正“自由”地游玩，还是只是在执行预设程序允许的选择？我不知道，因为恶魔被困在数据之中，而我被困在此刻。
